messages:
Priya: Heads-up: I finished a first draft of the multi-cloud refkit + terraform modules that target our marketplace partners. Includes Azure/GCP/AWS variants and a lightweight sandbox overlay for partner trials. Need eyes on publishing flow.
Diego: nice. Can you confirm how you handle provider blocks? partners usually want a single module that conditionally sets providers vs separate modules per cloud.
Priya: implemented as a root module that calls cloud-specific child modules. Root accepts `cloud = "aws|gcp|azure"` and exposes a small compatible interface. Docs show both patterns so partners can choose.
Hannah: for marketplace registry we need an artefact with automatic docs. Did you include terraform-docs + a changelog generator?
Priya: yes: pipeline builds docs with terraform-docs, then registry-bot (via GitHub Actions) creates a release and uploads the artifact tarball with CHECKSUMS and CHANGELOG.md generated from commit messages following our Conventional Commits pattern.
registry-bot: note: release pipeline configured -> preview artifacts will be published to staging-registry.redwood-inference.com on tag v0.1.0-rc.1
Diego: sandbox overlay sounds great. Does it include quota-limited service accounts and a teardown policy? partners hate accidental charges.
Priya: sandbox creates a small project/rg/subscription with a TTL (default 4h). The CI job runs deploy -> smoke tests -> destroy. TTL enforced by a background cleanup job we provide as a tiny cloud function.
Yara: important: include a short section on billing metrics export so partners can wire cost dashboards. A sample prometheus exporter + Grafana dashboard would help.
Priya: added prometheus export example and a grafana/dashboard.json under examples/monitoring. Also included a billing export snippet for GCP BigQuery and AWS Cost & Usage Report quickstart.
Hannah: Security/registry ask: add a pre-publish scanner step for license compliance and secret detection. We should fail the release if forbidden licenses found.
Priya: added an actions step that runs license-checker and truffleHog; flagged issues create GitHub issues automatically.
Diego: how are container images handled? marketplace partners often want a minimal base image and reproducible build.
Priya: we build distroless-based images via a reproducible build action + push signed images to our registry with cosign signatures. Documented in docs/image_policy.md.
Yara: for partner onboarding we should have a templated checklist: legal signoff, security review, marketplace metadata, support contacts, and a preflight test matrix. Can you add that in the repo under PARTNER_ONBOARDING.md?
Priya: done. PARTNER_ONBOARDING.md includes the preflight matrix: install path, upgrade path, revert path, and known-issues table.
registry-bot: ci/build #879: terraform fmt/validate/pass; image build queued
Hannah: quick ask: add an example of publishing modules to the Terraform Registry (public) vs hosting our own module registry for partners who want private control. We need docs on pros/cons.
Priya: added a short section: publish-public.md vs private-registry.md with screenshots and sample API tokens/permissions.
Diego: can we schedule a 45-minute walkthrough with CloudPartner next Wed? would like to demo the sandbox and the publish flow.
Yara: Wed works for me. Prefer 11am PT.
Priya: creating calendar invite now and will attach a short demo script and the repo link in the invite. PR coming tonight with README updates, examples, and the release pipeline yml. Please review for any blocker items.
Hannah: I'll focus on the security and license checks in the PR review. Diego please cover the multi-arch images. Yara will validate the onboarding doc.
Priya: thanks all. Final note: check examples/bootstrap-ampere.sh for the small kernel module step (non-blocking) and examples/quickstart-sandbox.sh for the deploy/test/destroy workflow.
Diego: LGTM, will review. :thumbsup:
